name: DecisionRules
description:
This MCP server exposes the authoring and execution surface for decision tables, lookup tables, and scripting rules directly to AI agents.

With it, an agent can:

Create and update decision tables, lookup tables, and scripting rules, including folder structure, tags, and versioning.
Evaluate (solve) any published or draft rule against real input data and get the decision output back.
Run and manage automated test suites against rules before publishing.
Check dependencies between rules, find duplicate decision-table rows, and lock rule versions to prevent accidental edits.
Use a built-in AI-authoring tool to generate a decision table, lookup table, or scripting rule from a plain-language description.

This makes it possible to go from "describe the business logic" to "a tested, versioned, live rule" without leaving the chat.

_published_faq.name: How do I add DecisionRules to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add DecisionRules to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.decisionrules.io/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the DecisionRules MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: DecisionRules lists 60 MCP tools, including add_tags_to_item, add_tags_to_item_version, create_folder, create_folder_by_path, create_rule, create_rule_version, create_space, create_test, create_test_suites, delete_folder_tree, delete_folder_tree_by_path, and delete_latest_rule.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to DecisionRules?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to DecisionRules in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Epicure, Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, and StatCite.
DecisionRules requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
DecisionRules is developed by DecisionRules. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
